keep: Means and ends are one claim: a just society cannot be built by unjust methods.
lede: A shy, unremarkable lawyer who failed in his first practice.
copy: Gandhi found himself in South Africa and there began developing the weapon that would define his life: satyagraha, the disciplined, non-violent resistance to injustice. Returning to India, he transformed the independence movement from an elite debating society into a mass struggle of hundreds of millions.

Through the Salt March, hunger strikes and the deliberate courting of arrest, he made the moral cost of empire impossible to ignore, and helped end British rule over a fifth of humanity without raising an army. He insisted on the unity of means and ends — that a just society cannot be built by unjust methods — and lived with radical simplicity, spinning his own cloth and reducing his needs to almost nothing.

He was not a saint and did not claim to be; his views on caste, sex and his own family invite hard criticism. Yet his method directly inspired the American civil rights movement, the anti-apartheid struggle and democratic uprisings worldwide. He was killed by a Hindu extremist for preaching reconciliation between Hindus and Muslims.

bio.t: Gandhi Before India & Gandhi: The Years That Changed the World
bio.why: India's leading historian wrote the definitive modern two-volume life, built on archives across four continents. It neither worships nor debunks. Gandhi's own Story of My Experiments with Truth (1929) remains essential first-hand reading.

contested: Guha is sympathetic, and the sharpest critique of Gandhi comes from a direction he handles gently: B. R. Ambedkar's argument that Gandhi's approach to caste protected the system it claimed to reform. Read Ambedkar's Annihilation of Caste, and Arundhati Roy's introduction to it, as the necessary counterweight.
